claim: Diario de Pernambuco reported on 23 June 2026 that Cais do Porto has been active since 2024 and that more than 45 Brazilian companies, most from Pernambuco, have used it.
In June 2026, a second group of ten Pernambuco companies arrived through Porto Digital's internationalisation programme, as DN Brasil reported on 22 June.
On 30 June, Porto Digital, Cais do Porto and CONSECTI signed a cooperation agreement, as reported by TI Inside.
In November 2024, Brazil's ambassador to Portugal, Raimundo Carreiro Silva, wrote in DN that Porto Digital Europa had chosen Aveiro's innovation hub and already had ten companies on board.
Sebrae's president, Décio Lima, signed a memorandum of understanding with Startup Portugal on 13 November 2023 during Web Summit.
ApexBrasil's Lisbon startup incubator, run with Sebrae, named its first class of ten startups at Web Summit 2025.
The next class of the ApexBrasil and Sebrae Lisbon incubator is due to be announced at the Brazil Pavilion on 10 November.
Unicorn Factory Lisboa's head, Gil Azevedo, told ECO in April 2025 that the hub has three signed partnerships with Brazilian hubs: Instituto Caldeira, Cubo and Sai do Papel.

ApexBrasil reports Brazil's ecosystem has more than 13,000 startups, more than 120 venture capital funds, more than 250 innovation hubs and more than 30 unicorns, as Brasil 61 reported on 31 August 2026.
Brazilian venture capital totalled US$2.135 billion in 2024 across 386 deals, according to ApexBrasil's own survey as reported by Brasil 61.
Invest.Rio and Maravalley are bringing ten Rio de Janeiro startups to this year's Web Summit.
Gol has opened its first intercontinental route, from Rio de Janeiro to Lisbon.
